newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors grill leading lawmaker on Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors grill leading lawmaker on Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Friday began questioning a prominent opposition lawmaker at the start of an inquiry into a group of politicians alleged to have taken money from the founder of the troubled Hanbo Group, a prosecution official said.

Kim Yong-hwan, secretary-general of the United Liberal Democrats, one of the two main opposition parties, is among 33 politicians the prosecutors said they would investigate in connection with a loans scandal involving Hanbo.
Hanbo Founder Chung Tae-soo and his aides have told prosecutors that they gave money to 20 lawmakers and 13 others as "political funds" but denied bribing them, senior prosecutor Shim Je-ryoon said.

Prosecutors said another opposition member of parliament, Kim Sang-hyun of the National Congress for New Politics, had agreed to report to the prosecution office for questioning on Friday over the scandal.

Among the 20 lawmakers are 13 from the ruling New Korea Party, including Kim Deog-ryong, a member of President Kim Young-sam's inner circle. He would probably report to the prosecution on Saturday, they said.
The prosecutors charged that Chung had bribed politicians and bankers to keep loans rolling into Hanbo's steelmaking flagship, which collapsed in January.
